content.thinking:
I'm planning out the body's 3D coordinate system, defining the floor height, hip root position, and spine path points to build the skeletal structure.

I continue adding neck joints and the head position, then realize the head placement is pushing the total height taller than intended, so I'm adjusting the hip and spine heights downward to keep proportions balanced with the mohawk included.

Now I'm working out leg geometry — hip and ball joint positions, segment lengths, and the distance they need to span. Since the available slack is loose relative to reach, I'm figuring out how the knee should bend forward in a digitigrade stance with the lower leg running roughly parallel to the root-to-target direction.

I'll fall back to a simpler rule where every joint turns by the same angle instead. For mass, I'm tapering the leg radii from thigh down to metatarsus, and starting to loft the torso and pelvis from spine chain stations with waist and hip widths defined.

Still writing torso loft stations...

Adding crease lines and ab segmentation via skin paint function, then starting head joint placement at [0,2.05,0.52] aimed slightly downward-forward.

I'm figuring out how the local coordinate helper treats left/right offsets relative to the head's facing direction, then deciding to just compute side points directly from absolute coordinates using the head's position and forward/up axes instead of relying on ambiguous word conventions.

Now I'm defining a helper `hp(l,u,f)` that converts left/up/forward offsets into model-space vectors from the head joint, and starting to lay out the head geometry — placing the cranium sphere with specific offsets and flattened radii to create a sloped forehead shape.

Continuing the face layout, I'm positioning heavy brow ridge capsules angled down and outward for a strong overhang, darkening the skin tone there, then placing amber glowing eye spheres with dark pupils nested in recessed eye sockets, and adding angled upper eyelid capsules to give a scowling expression before moving on to shaping the snout and midface.

Now I'm sculpting a long hooked nose using a tapered sweep from the brow bridge down to a pointed tip, adding small dark nostril spheres beneath it, then building the upper lip and maxilla as wide tapering boxes, cheekbone spheres on either side, and starting on the lower jaw joint placement.

Writing jaw mesh and mouth parts...

Adding a gold ring bracelet on one tusk plus small upper canines, then working out the ears as extruded leaf-shaped outlines angled back and up, defining the ear plane's direction vectors so the thickness extrudes correctly.

Now I'm planning the mohawk crest as a curved path along the skull descending into the neck, with individual spikes swept along that path at intervals, each angled upward and back with tapering length via bezier sweeps.

I'll extend the mohawk crest with about 13 spikes staying within the head region, plus a few smaller spikes skinned onto the neck bones for continuity. I also want to add facial details like warts, scars, and warpaint decals across the cheeks, nose, and shoulders.

Now I'm working out the decal projection onto the cranium sphere for tribal face paint stripes, plus a chest tattoo decal, and thinking about teeth as individual cone-shaped spike parts along the jaw rather than merged geometry since each part stays within the overall part limit.

I'm sketching a `bits` helper that merges multiple transformed geometries into a single part per bone, then moving on to plan the bone fetish necklace — a looped string of points around the neck and clavicles dropping toward the chest, defined as a closed Catmull-Rom path.

For decoration I'm planning pendants (bones, teeth, claws, and a central glowing-eyed skull) hung from points along the loop, plus tiny alternating turquoise/bone/red beads spaced along the path. Next I'm designing a left shoulder pauldron built from an alligator skull — cranium box, elongated snout frustum, cone teeth, eye sockets — wrapped with leather straps and moss.

I'm sizing the gator skull and angling it forward and outward on the right shoulder bone, then adding three curved rib-bone spikes on the left shoulder tied with leather and a feathered, beaded bundle. For the hip belt, I'm working through how the loop plane should be oriented relative to the hips/spine joint's default axis so the cut forms a clean horizontal band around the waist.

Now I'm setting the belt to tilt slightly for a hunched look, defining it as a literal frame rather than tied to a bone joint, with a slight lift so it clears the thigh geometry properly. For the buckle I'm adding a large skull plate at the front belt hit, and for the loincloth I'm considering extruding a cloth flap downward from the belt with a tribal pattern, possibly using a textured card hanging at the front.

Double-sided cards with alpha cutout work well for ragged flap edges, so I'm planning the loincloth front, back, and side tassels as painted tribal cards with slight bend for curvature rather than flat extrudes, since extrudes give volume but cards allow finer painted detail like stitches and frayed edges. Around the belt I'm adding a skirt of ragged moss and hide strips as a ring of about 14 varied-length tinted cards, giving that swamp-troll grass-skirt feel with bone beads mixed in.

Hanging items off the belt: a stitched voodoo doll with pins and a bone rattle totem on the left hip, a studded femur club, a drawstring pouch, and a bundle of teeth on the right. For the back totem I'm building a pole with small skulls, teal and red feather cards, beaded dangling strings, and a glowing green gem, plus a diagonal bandolier strap draped from right shoulder to left hip with beads and rivets following a rough path across the chest.

For limb accessories I'm setting up bone-bead cuffs as loops around the bicep joints, striped cloth wrist wraps with claws, and knee/ankle bone rings by sweeping a loop profile through a cutting plane at each leg joint.

Now I'm adding skin surface details -- warts, scars, dark spot decals, and moss patches painted where the surface normal faces upward and noise is high, giving a swamp-worn look on the shoulders, back, and head, plus muddy coloring on the lower legs. I'm scattering moss tufts, ferns, tiny mushrooms, and hanging Spanish moss cards off the pauldron bones, darkening the claws to a dirty bone tone, making the eyes glow, and shading the skin with gradient-based painted shadows that darken toward the underside of each form for that saturated Warcraft-style look.

I'm defining one unified skin paint function that mixes base dark and light tones by surface orientation and noise, layering in belly paleness, moss, mud, and warts so the whole body reads as a continuous painted surface rather than disjointed parts. Given the body's surface area, I'm bumping the paint resolution to 2048 (atlas to 4096) to keep texel density sharp enough for facial and linework detail, and I'm capping the palette at 64 flat colors to match the stylized look.

For the face, I'm giving the eyes an amber glow with a small flattened dark pupil sphere offset slightly forward. For the mouth, I'm building the jaw as a separate hinged piece so it can open, and posing it a few degrees forward at rest to show teeth and tongue for a more menacing default expression, applying that pose after the jaw and teeth are constructed so the hierarchy stays intact.

I'm also considering small details like a gold nose ring through the septum, knuckle bumps on the hands via small spheres, and cloth wrist wraps with striped coloring looped around the forearm.

For the wrist wraps I'm planning to find a surface loop around a point on the arm sweep — using a frame at a given point along the chain to get a plane perpendicular to the limb, then creating a closed sweep path from that loop with a small radius and slight lift.

I should also name key parts for easier preview queries, keep triangle counts low (sphere segments around 190 tris, total cap at 60k), and flesh out the tusks as a central swamp-troll feature — big, curved, ivory with stained rings, one chipped, one gold-capped. Time to write the actual code, importing the glow kit and keeping only what's needed.

I'm building helper functions for creating transformed geometries and merging them with Three.js utilities — a vector helper, a piece-placement function using matrix composition from position/rotation/scale, and verifying that all primitive geometries share consistent indexed attributes so they merge cleanly. I'm also working out whether paint colors applied via UV coordinates will read correctly in model space once pieces are merged at the origin.

Now I'm sketching the actual skeleton coordinates for the troll rig, starting with the builder setup and hips joint position, then defining the spine chain as a Catmull-Rom curve through several points with named sub-bones, and beginning the neck chain extending upward and forward from the top of the spine.

Continuing, I'm defining the head joint parented to the neck's last bone with an orientation pointing slightly down and forward, then setting up a helper function to compute positions relative to the head in local space for placing facial features. From there I'm starting the jaw joint, positioned below the head and aimed down-forward, and working out where to anchor the rest of the head's contents relative to this new reference point.

Now I'm checking the cranium's placement — the head sits ahead of the chest by about 0.3 meters, giving a forward-thrust, hunched troll posture, which looks right. I'm adding a trapezius hump as a flattened sphere near the neck base, then moving into blocking out the torso loft stations, defining widths and heights at the pelvis and waist levels to shape the body's silhouette.

Checking the shoulder joint sits just outside the loft width, with the deltoid sphere covering it properly alongside the trapezius. Now I'm mapping out the arm chain coordinates from shoulder to elbow to wrist.

Computing the upper arm and forearm lengths, the fingertips land near knee height, which matches troll proportions with arms hanging to the knees. I'm also verifying the wrist stays clear of the thigh radius so the arms don't clip through the legs, then starting the catmull curve for the arm sweep.

Now I'm setting up the arm chain with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints parented to the third spine joint, and defining a radius taper function along the arm path—thicker near the shoulder, tapering through the elbow, then slightly thickening again for the forearm.

Then I'm placing the hand palm as a sphere positioned below the wrist, and computing the hand's orientation axes by normalizing the direction from elbow to wrist so I can build fingers aligned along that direction.

Still working out finger curl directions...

Fingers spaced along z with offsets, thumb on the forward side pointing down-forward, and I'm sizing the palm sphere with thickness, length, and width scales while curling inward along x. Thinking of a simpler rest pose akin to a loose T-pose for the limb.

Now I'm defining finger joint chains: base point plus offsets, then successive spans using direction vectors with small x-curl shifts, naming joints like `indexL1` through `indexL3` under the wrist parent, using catmull splines across three spans per finger.

For claws, I'm placing a spike at the fingertip, oriented along the final span's direction with slight curl, sized small and colored as claw tissue, attached to the last finger joint. Then I'm sweeping the finger chain with a tapering radius profile and rounded caps to form the finger shape itself.

Now I'm working out the feet: positioning a ball joint and building three forward-angled toe chains (center, inner, outer) each with two tapering segments, keeping the toe radius roughly constant so the tube sits flush against the ground.

For the legs, I'm planning to chain four joints per leg (hip, knee, hock, ball) and sketch a claw spike angled forward-down off each toe tip.

For leg thickness I'm tapering the radius smoothly from thigh down to the ball of the foot, with a slight calf bulge, and the hip joint will sit as the root point.

Now I'm setting up the color palette constants for the skin tones before writing the main build function.

Defining skin paint function using layered noise...

Adding belly shading, moss patches near the top, mud blending near the base, and blotchy wart-like spots using cell noise...

I'm defining the color function to return a readonly Rgb tuple, then separately designing the ivory tusk gradient from a dark root to a pale tip with subtle grooves and cooler highlights, plus planning the hair, leather, and cloth paint treatments and considering which parts should use SVG textures instead.

Still writing texture specs...

I'll also sketch a skull helper function that builds cranium, jaw, eye sockets, and teeth geometry, oriented using a bone frame and position/direction parameters for reuse in fetishes and totems.

Continuing the skull geometry: upper and lower jaw boxes positioned and sized relative to s, dark eye socket spheres with optional glow, small cone teeth along jaw edges, and optional brow horn spikes for certain creature variants.

I'll merge bone-colored parts into single geometries per skull, keeping teeth and sockets as separate tinted meshes, and build a reusable helper that composes transforms (translation, rotation, scale in local frame plus a global orientation) to place each piece before merging — enough to construct a dozen or so skulls affordably.

I'm considering flat shading tradeoffs—applying it to bony or angular parts like teeth for a faceted low-poly feel, but keeping skin and rounded forms smooth to match the hand-painted Warcraft aesthetic.

For rings, I'll use a torus geometry with a modest radial segment count to keep the low-poly look consistent.

Now I'm setting up the file structure: defining metadata for the creature (name, description, style, commit) and importing the necessary Three.js utilities, builder helpers, math functions, and curve tools to start constructing the troll piece by piece.

Writing more imports and defining a color palette for the swamp troll's skin, moss, mud, and warts, then building a paint function that blends these colors using noise to create the mottled skin texture.

Blending in a pale belly patch based on normal direction and vertical position, then adding horizontal ab lines across the belly region for a subtle muscle-line detail.

Now I'm layering moss growth on top-facing surfaces using noise thresholds, blending between two moss color variants, and starting on a mud layer that darkens the lower surfaces based on height and additional noise.

Checking whether moss would incorrectly appear on the head top under the mohawk versus the face — moss is restricted to upward-facing normals so it should be fine. I'm skipping extra edge-darkening for the Warcraft style and moving to the hair paint function, which blends a dark red base into orange along the strand, then shifts toward yellow near the tip.

Now I'm defining the tusk paint, blending tan to cream along the length, adding brighter tip color, periodic ring grooves from a sine pattern, and subtle stain streaks using noise weighted toward the base. For bones, I'm setting up a mottled light-and-dark bone coloring pattern with a small mottle size.

I'm sketching the leather paint as a grain pattern along the x-axis before settling on a mottle approach instead, then starting to build the actual skeleton code -- defining the builder, the hips joint, and a spine chain following a catmull-rom path through three spine segments.

Now I'm extending the chain upward: adding a neck chain with two segments branching from the chest joint, then a head joint positioned above the neck with its own direction vector. I'm treating head.local as a helper for defining local axes, and I'm about to move on to building out the torso.

For the torso, I'm lofting through four stations with varying widths and heights along the same spine path, attaching it to the hips and spine bones with ten sides for smoothness. Then I'm setting up a neck sweep using the neck chain's path, sizing its radius to blend into the trapezius area where it meets the torso.

For the head, I'm defining a helper to position features in head-local space, then building a cranium sphere scaled into an oval shape and attached to the head bone, confirming the scale property accepts array values based on kit documentation. I'm starting work on the brow geometry next, using capsule shapes positioned symmetrically off the head's center.

I'm reconsidering the brow slant for a scowling, troll-like expression — flipping the inner and outer height values so the inner brow sits lower, giving a heavier, angrier look. I'm then building the eyes: a glowing sphere for the iris, a darker larger sphere behind it as the socket, and starting on a tiny pupil shape.

Adding eyelid and snout geometry...

Still placing nose details...

Now I'm adding the mouth cavity as a dark red box recessed between the muzzle and jaw, then placing small conical fangs along the upper lip, and starting the lower jaw geometry with a frustum loft down to the chin point.

Still placing jaw features...

Setting the torus's orientation along the tusk's tangent direction. I'm also planning ears via extrusion, scattering warts across the cranium and jaw, and adding a small braided chin tendril with a bead hanging below the jaw. For the mohawk, I'm thinking through placing hair cards along the crest frames, sized and angled to flow upward and back.

For the necklace I'm plotting a closed loop of points dipping low in front near the chest and rising around the sides and back of the neck, so a catmull spline through them will drape naturally like a chain.

This drape then needs to project onto the nearest body surface (torso, neck, trapezius) so the cord follows the body's contours, and I'll sweep a thin tube along it with beads placed at sampled points along the path, grouped into a few color sets. Pendants get positioned at specific parameter values along the front-center of the loop to hang centered with smaller ones spaced outward.

Now I'm working out the shoulder pauldron placement, computing the gator-skull center position relative to the shoulder joint and deltoid radius, and figuring out the forward-out-up orientation vector so the skull snout points away from the body correctly.

On the opposite shoulder I'm adding curved bone spikes along a bezier arc, wrapped with leather torus rings and hanging feather bundles with beads. Then I'm positioning the belt loop by finding the torso loft station near y≈1.2 so the leather strap wraps cleanly around the hip transition before moving into the thigh geometry.

Pushing the belt up to y 1.36 risks clipping the belly sphere, which bulges past the loft surface — so the belt loop needs to sit outside the belly, meaning I should fold the belly into the torso target rather than treat it separately, or adjust the loft stations to already account for its width.

Since the loft centers don't have to match the spine chain exactly, I can offset each station's center forward independently: pelvis, belly, chest, and shoulders each get their own position, width, and height to shape the pot-belly profile directly in the loft rather than via a separate shift function.

Now I'm figuring out how to add a belt as a loop or swept band around the torso, positioning it between the pelvis and belly stations and working out how to orient the belt's cross-section relative to the path's tangent, normal, and binormal so the band sits flat and horizontal around the body.

I also need to locate the front-facing point on the belt path to anchor a buckle or skull decoration, searching for the parameter where the path is closest to the forward direction, and plan attaching loincloth flap frames at that same front point.

Thinking about orientation: with the frame leaning 180° and flow pointing downward, the cards hang with the root edge at the top and the tip pointing down, so viewed from downstream the drawing would appear upside down unless I account for this when laying out the texture.

A 180° rotation preserves handedness so symmetric patterns won't be affected, and since the card is double-sided with its plane perpendicular to the flow, I'll draw the cloth upright in normal orientation (waistband top, ragged hem bottom) and then apply a rotation transform to flip it into the correct downstream orientation.

Now I'm placing accessories: a bone club on the right hip of the belt, a voodoo doll on the left, plus a pouch. For the totem pole rising from the lower back, I'm positioning it from the lumbar region leaning up behind the head to around chest height, riding along the spine, and adding a harness with a bandolier strap crossing from shoulder to opposite hip to anchor it alongside the belt.

I'm working out the stacked skulls decorating the pole, considering their height and orientation so they read correctly from the front without disappearing behind the head or mohawk, given how the pole and crest overlap in depth.

I'll have skulls facing forward, visible above the head, and add a crossbar with hanging charms, a feather bundle, and a glowing green gem on the top skull for a shaman-totem silhouette, attaching everything to the chest bone. I'm also noting to check that arm placement doesn't conflict with other bone-mounted items like hip gear.

Now I'm working out hanging positions for belt items like a voodoo doll or club, avoiding overlap with the thigh and knee as the character swings their arm near the elbow.

I'm planning the overall code structure, aiming for a compact ~600-700 lines with helper functions to construct pieces, pack them together, and build skull-like shapes with directional glow options for the shoulder bone items.

Working out skull geometry proportions...

Also planning glowing eye sockets, teeth cones, and SVG gradient textures for a hair tuft effect.

Still designing more textures: a feather pattern with teal vanes and red tips, moss strands, a tribal tattoo decal, and facepaint stripes, before moving into writing the decal placement code with target, direction, and size parameters.

For the chest, I'm deciding to drop separate pec spheres and instead rely on shading plus a decal applied across the combined torso and pec surface for definition, then starting to write the helper function.

Writing arm/hand chains...

Writing finger geometry code...

Still building thumb and finger chains...

Confirming limb's parameter structure works for four points with three lengths and two bends. I'm adding knee caps as spheres at the knee joint, a foot pad sphere at the ball positioned so its bottom sits flush with the floor, and planning toe chains branching from the leg tip.

Still writing toe geometry...

I'm also thinking about adding a heel spur spike, muddy skin tones on the soles, and a rounded butt shape for the loincloth area. Then I'll move on to building armbands as loops along the arm's tangent frames.

Now I'm adding bone bead cuffs along the loop path, plus forearm wraps in dirty tan cloth and a wrist bracelet with claw details, then similar wrap loops at the knee.

Next I'm placing ankle bone rings further along the leg path, and planning chest straps with a bandolier pouch. For scatter decoration, I'm adding moss tufts using surface hit detection filtered by normal and height, rendering them as leaning card textures, then starting on the mohawk crest path.

Still mapping skull coordinates for the crest...

Still shaping spike geometry...

Still shaping ear geometry...

I'm also planning a gold torus earring at the lobe position, deciding whether to add a face decal later, and double-checking the part option types like bone, scale, dir, and flat before continuing to write the piece definitions.

Now I'm working out the totem pole geometry: a tapered wooden rod from base to top with grain-colored paint, then placing a stack of skulls at intervals along its length with varying sizes and orientations so they don't overlap awkwardly.

I'm adding a crossbar with hanging feather fans and beaded strings, plus leather harness straps that wrap from the pole base over the shoulders and across the chest like a bandolier, making sure the arms won't clip through them. Now I'm drafting the loincloth as an SVG shape in its own viewBox, oriented upright and rotated into place.

Writing SVG shape details...

Finishing the feather with teal and orange coloring, then moving to the moss blades and hair tuft flame shapes with their orange-red gradient fills. With the glow effect imported, I'm ready to write the final file.

input.command: mkdir -p scratch/swampTroll samples && ls samples | head; grep -n "export" src/builder.ts | head -30
